schemes.name: sawtooth_hall_stands_tall
schemes.secondary_language: one tall bar, six storeys, its top cut into three parallel gabled bays - a sawtooth crown read from the street as three ridges in a row
schemes.formal_principle: The north neighbour's daylight envelope allows height only along the street edge, so the program stacks into one tall bar there; a single ridge across a bar this wide would be a tent, so the roof breaks into three bays - each bay a house-sized ridge, the crown reading as a row of houses carried six storeys up.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a tall bar wearing three ridges

ops.why: Input: the daylight envelope leaves height only at the street edge, and the program wants six storeys - so one bar takes them all. Limit: height 0.9 with storeys 6 declares tall; the bar is one plain body and the next word gives it a top.

Input: a 45-degree ridge over a body this wide would eat two storeys, so the roof splits across the long axis into three bays, each with its own ridge at a run a house would have. Limit: pitch 1.0 is the honest 45 degrees; three bays keep each run under the 1.5-storey roof cap so the silhouette shows three real ridges, not one shallow parapet.

schemes.name: gabled_ring_around_a_court
schemes.secondary_language: four four-storey bars ringing a court, every bar under its own 45-degree ridge - a village street wrapped into a square
schemes.formal_principle: The FAR wants the parcel filled deep and a deep plate goes dark, so the rooms gather as four bars around a court; each bar is narrow enough to carry a real pitched roof, so the ring reads from outside as four gabled houses joined at the corners and from the court as one continuous eave.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a court ring of gabled houses

ops.why: Input: depth kills daylight, so the mass rings a court and every room gets two fronts. Limit: bar 0.22 keeps each bar narrow enough for a pitched roof to be a roof; height 0.6 with storeys 4 declares mid.

Input: a flat-topped ring is a block with a hole; the four narrow bars are exactly the bodies a 45-degree ridge belongs to. Limit: pitch 1.0 on a bar 0.22 of the parcel wide lands inside the roof cap, so all four ridges draw fully and meet at the corners.

schemes.name: houses_bear_on_a_plinth
schemes.secondary_language: a two-storey plinth the full parcel wide, and on it a smaller two-storey house under one steep ridge - the roof only where the house is
schemes.formal_principle: The street asks for a continuous low wall while the program has one tall room it wants to show, so the wall becomes a plinth and the room a house set back on top: the ridge belongs to the house alone, the plinth stays flat and public, and the section reads as ground floor city, upper floor home.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a house set back on a plinth

ops.why: Input: the street edge wants a continuous low wall and the program has one room it wants to lift above it. Stack two tiers with contrast 2.2 so the upper is a house on a plinth, aligned back so the plinth's street face stays whole. Limit: storeys 2 sizes each tier as a two-storey unit.

Input: the house on top wants a roof and the plinth does not - a roof over the plinth would make the street wall a barn. The ridge lands only on the tier nothing stands on. Limit: 45 degrees on the narrow upper tier stays inside the cap and reads as a house.

schemes.name: tall_house_row_on_a_plinth
schemes.secondary_language: a plinth and a tall four-storey block above it under a row of three ridges - the upper block a terrace of houses in the sky
schemes.formal_principle: Density asks for height at the back of the parcel while the front must stay low, so a three-storey base carries a taller block set back from the street, and the tall block is roofed as three gabled bays so its bulk reads as a row of houses rather than one slab.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a terrace of houses lifted on a base

ops.why: Input: height belongs at the back, away from the street's low neighbours. Two tiers, the upper set back, contrast 1.4 so the upper block is still a full building. Limit: height 0.95 with storeys 4 per tier declares tall.
Input: the upper block is wide; one ridge would be shallow, three bays give it three real ridges. Limit: bays 3 keeps each run under the roof cap; the roof lands only on the top tier.

schemes.name: five_tall_houses_in_a_field

schemes.formal_principle: The program is five separate tenancies and the parcel has no dominant edge, so the building is five tall houses standing apart in a field: each house is its own address with its own ridge, and the space between them is the building's real room - a yard passing under no roof at all.

schemes.name: upper_tier_lifted_off_the_base

schemes.name: houses_in_the_air

schemes.name: mansard_bar_holds_the_street
schemes.secondary_language: one four-storey street bar with the top storey inside a steep mansard - the eave at three storeys, the roof inhabited

schemes.name: vaulted_ring_stands_tall

schemes.name: terraces_step_down_to_the_open
